task_description: Write a method in Dafny that takes in a list of string and a string and inserts the string before each element in the list, and returns the resulting list.
specification_response:
Method Signature:
    method InsertBeforeEach(lst: seq<string>, s: string) returns (result: seq<string>)
Postconditions_prompt:
    - The resulting sequence contains twice as many elements as the input list
- For each original element in the input list, the corresponding element in the result sequence is the string s followed by the original element
- The order of the original elements is preserved, with s inserted immediately before each of them
code_response:
Step 1: Determine the method’s signature.  
In this case:  
    method InsertBeforeEach(lst: seq<string>, s: string) returns (result: seq<string>)  

Step 2: Determine the preconditions.  
In this case:  
Natural language description:  
    - There are no preconditions; the method works for any list of strings and any string.  
Dafny specification:  
    // No preconditions required

Step 3: Determine the postconditions.  
In this case:  
Natural language description:  
    - The resulting list has length equal to twice the input list length  
    - For each index i in the result, if i is even, result[i] is the string s, and if i is odd, result[i] is the element from lst at position i/2  
    - The order of original elements in lst is preserved at the odd indices in result

Dafny specification:  
    ensures |result| == 2 * |lst|  
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==>  
        (i % 2 == 0 ==> result[i] == s) &&  
        (i % 2 == 1 ==> result[i] == lst[i/2])  

Step 4: Write the code, its formal specification, and the verification annotations that help the solver prove the postconditions.  
In this case:

```dafny
method InsertBeforeEach(lst: seq<string>, s: string) returns (result: seq<string>)
    ensures |result| == 2 * |lst|
    ensures forall i :: 0 <= i < |result| ==> 
        (i % 2 == 0 ==> result[i] == s) &&
        (i % 2 == 1 ==> result[i] == lst[i/2])
{
    var res := [];
    var i := 0;
    while i < |lst|
        invariant 0 <= i <= |lst|
        invariant |res| == 2 * i
        {
            // Append s before lst[i]
            res := res + [s, lst[i]];
            i := i + 1;
        }
    result := res;
}
```
